analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 10, 2026)
key_insights: Sales commentary, not research. Futures flat pre-CPI (SPX +0.0%, NDX -0.3%, RTY +0.0%), with Tech lower after the recent Tech selloff and rebound. 10Y at 4.886%, VIX at 20.01, WTI -189bps at $85.21.
The yield curve is flattening, with the 2Y yield up 5bp, possibly reacting to Waller's comment that a 50bp hike may be needed if CPI prints hot.
JPM Market Intel says the Waller comment is a bit surprising given the relatively sanguine Fed commentary of recent months. Today's CPI will help solidify December Fed expectations.
Jay Barry had flagged that the 2Y yield was about 25bp too low versus model-based valuation, so the curve may flatten near-term. The desk says that move tends to support Secular Growth and Mag7.

The market is trading as though the US/Iran conflict is ending, which would be a disinflationary tailwind. The desk asks whether the market reacts to a hot print or assumes the Fed looks through inflation induced by Strait of Hormuz constraints.

After yesterday's broad Everything Rally, the desk's tactical Tech preference is hyperscalers as the preferred long. It cites ongoing challenges for the picks-and-shovels part of the AI trade (financing, monetization, valuation).
Feroli expects headline CPI +0.25% MoM (3.9% YoY) and core +0.23% MoM (3.2% YoY). For PPI he expects headline +0.6% MoM (6.8% YoY) and core +0.4% MoM (5.1% YoY).

Jay Barry notes September CPI was the third upside surprise in the last 12 releases and, at 7bp, the largest since March 2024. Inflation data over the past month surprised the most to the upside since May 2021, even with 10-year breakevens down 13bp.
JPM expects core CPI of +0.23% m/m, in line with consensus and above market pricing of 0.21%. It sees this as potential support for inflation markets.

JPM Rates Trading gives one-day CPI breakevens (straddle struck at 11am, expiring 11am Tuesday): SFRZ6 2.50bp, SFRZ7 8.375bp, SFRZ8 7.75bp, FV 6.75bp, 5y 6.375bp, TY 6.00bp, 10y 5.00bp, US 4.50bp, 30y 4.00bp.

JPM Center for Geopolitics describes three Middle East scenarios: an 'Epic Fury 2.0' repeating the spring's military targets, broader attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure, or a performative 'final blow' on a nuclear target. Washington has had these options since the MOU collapsed in June and has not used them, given the risk of Iranian retaliation.

JPM Commodity Trading puts 50% on further strikes followed by a declaration that military action is over. Of that, 75% is that the US keeps a presence to secure Hormuz and continues the blockade, and 25% is that it withdraws.

In the 75% branch Brent opens about $3 higher but ends unchanged to $2 lower, with prices near $90 longer term. In the 25% branch it opens unchanged, falls about $4 as positions are exited, then recovers to $105-110 within a week.
The other 50% is that diplomacy is given more time. JPM Commodity Trading expects a $4-5 price decline and a 7-10 point fall in volatility through the week as investors exit January length.
Ian Mitchell (Energy) says the desk sees no chance of the wider re-escalation scenarios materialising this weekend, and he agrees.
Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 on $365 EPS at 21.9x, implying 8.4% upside from Friday's close.

Dubravko attributes the pullback to a de-leveraging event. AI and AI-adjacent names were chased with record leverage, and liquidity began to dry up in late June. Systematic and vol strategies and buyside liquidations magnified it.
October was the largest single-month unwind for Long Momentum, down about 11% or 6 standard deviations. Momentum L/S fell about 40% from its peak.
Equity multiples compressed about 4x since January while earnings grew double digits. AI company multiples fell about 35% since May: Semis 52%, hyperscalers 14%, Memory 60%, Processing Units 50%.

Dubravko sees the selling as far along: Momentum crowding reset from 100th to 76th percentile, levered ETF sales of about $60bn Thursday and $35bn the prior Friday, CTAs flipped to net short with maybe $50bn left to sell, dealer net gamma imbalance at 12th percentile, $1.2T of announced buybacks, and QQQ RSI below 30 (average ~4% rally over the next five days).

Dubravko's catalysts: Middle East developments, MegaCap IPOs, next month's ERCOT meeting (AI capex implications) and the December Fed meeting. He sees the US midterms as a clearing event and data center headwinds as less onerous than priced.

Dubravko estimates every $100B of AI capex adds about $9 to 2027 S&P 500 EPS (~2.5% growth). Mid-range capex of ~$1.5T would add about $18 versus consensus, or 4-5% to 2027 EPS growth. JPM credit analysts expect hyperscalers to fund 2027 capex absent credit shocks, though the funding mix needs more equity.

Dubravko's trade ideas: (i) long 12M Momentum vs short 3M Momentum, essentially Tech vs Energy/Defensives; (ii) Low Vol less compelling, with Healthcare, then Utilities and Staples as the best Low Vol areas; (iii) AI Upstream attractive after the positioning flush; (iv) Consumer Cyclicals challenged by affordability, with longer-term value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail vs Energy.
On housing, Dubravko says mortgage rates need to approach 6.0% to see inflows into the group.
Macro view for 2027: JPM Economics expects US GDP growth to slow but stay trend-like with modest disinflation. Dubravko's team estimates EPS growth of about 20%.
Europe is higher (SX5E +1.1%, DAX +1.2%, UKX +0.3%), led by Italy and Spain, as the region benefits most from lower energy prices. APAC was strong (NKY +2.9%, KOSPI +4.4%, HSI +0.4%).
Today's US earnings: CAPR, CRWV, INO, LQDA, NN, QBTS, RGTI, SGRY, TDG, VG.
